verdicts.reasoning: What I read: TS BaseNode requires cornerSmoothing (src/lib/design/types.ts:484), and the schema defaults a missing key to 0 (schema.ts:332). Swift DesignNode has no such property, key, decode or encode (DesignDocument.swift:478-690). `rg cornerSmoothing -g '*.swift' native/` returns nothing; the only native hit is the bundled editor.js. The bridge decodes every transaction's document into this struct through DesignDocumentCodec.load (DesignBridge.swift:126-130), and JSONDecoder ignores unknown keys (DesignDocumentCodec.swift:54). DesktopDesignSurface re-encodes that struct into the draft (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1076-1080). The host is built from the decoded struct and sends openDocument from it (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:69-72, 158), so the editor never receives the value either. The server stores the body as-is (src/app/api/artifacts/[id]/route.ts:60-68), and the web later parses the missing key as 0, so the reset happens silently. My script comparing every field in types.ts against the Swift kit found cornerSmoothing as the only dropped node field; delayMs, easing and matchStableIds survive because they sit inside DesignJSONValue. No test fixture contains cornerSmoothing. The iPhone library also edits the latest version (JunoMobileWorkspaceViews.swift:2061-2068, readOnly only when the version is not the latest), so it loses the value the same way. High severity is justified: this is silent, document-wide data loss.

What I read: saveArtifact sends baseVersion from the `artifacts` array at the moment of saving (NativeArtifactStore.swift:321-335). reload() replaces that array after every sync (258-288). DesktopDesignSurface reads `content` once and ignores later values (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:973-979). The Design screen keys the surface only on design id plus the discard token (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:425-435) and never calls host.adopt. The server compares only baseVersion with currentVersion (route.ts:51-56) and accepts a whole-document replacement. So a v4 that sync brings in while v3 is on the canvas is overwritten by the next Save. On a 409, merge(latest) (NativeArtifactStore.swift:422-426) moves storedContent to the latest version but keeps the draft (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:574-582), and a second Save then overwrites. The stale message even claims 'The latest version has been loaded' (NativeArtifactAPIClient.swift:192-193), yet the canvas never shows it. Only Discard, which re-reads storedContent, would reveal v4.

What I read: the draft lives only in @State (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:215). 'All designs' calls closeDesign(), which clears it with no prompt (444-446, 520-523), and `.onAppear { closeDesign() }` runs as well (264). The screen is one arm of a switch (DesktopAccountScreens.swift:120-134), so changing destination destroys its state. There is no onDisappear, confirmationDialog or dirty guard in the file (rg found only the isDirty uses at 239/474/481/507). Across native/macOS I found no applicationShouldTerminate or isDocumentEdited handling for designs. Discard is also a single click with no confirmation (470-476).

verdicts.corrected_location: scripts/build-design-editor.mjs:190-202; .github/workflows/release-macos.yml and native.yml have no check; tests/design-host-bridge.test.ts:77
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by running it: `node scripts/build-design-editor.mjs --check` exits 1 with 'bundle is stale (expected 1.0.0+9cc1cfa8d4fe)', and index.html stamps 1.0.0+2b86e5baaf9d. The last bundle commit is 2fa09d35 (17 Sept). Eleven commits followed, touching src/components/design and icon-swap (1161+/491-), and the release commit 0a3087fe changed only version files. The shipped bundle lacks strings that bundled sources now contain: `after:scale-x-100` (design-editor.tsx:893) and `svg.icon[data-motion]` (host/editor.css:188) are both absent. The bridge test passes without comparing the hash. One correction: 'nothing in CI checks it' is wrong. .github/workflows/release-ios.yml:76 runs `npm run design:editor:check`, so the iOS production release is gated. The Mac release (release-macos.sh, release-macos.yml) and the per-push native.yml are not. Another caveat is that the hash covers all of src/lib/design, including server-only files, so some staleness reports may not affect the bundle. I lowered severity to medium: this is drift and missing fixes, not data loss.

What I read: Tailwind runs with `--content` limited to src/components/design/** plus icon-swap.tsx (build-design-editor.mjs:171-172). The shipped editor.css (25.8KB) has 0 matches for `display:inline-flex`, `.size-8{`, `.h-8{`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `surface-float`, `overlay-glass`, `z-popper`, `animate-pop-in`, `animate-tooltip-in`, `control-primary` and `.bg-selected`. The editor imports ui/tooltip 8×, ui/dropdown-menu 5×, menu-recipe 5×, ui/button 4× and popover/select/dialog/kbd. TooltipContent's only surface is `surface-float` (tooltip.tsx:59), and the menu shell is `surface-float overlay-glass z-popper …` (menu-recipe.ts:68-71). Those component classes are defined only in globals.css (1137, 1154, 1190, 1797), and the host editor.css (read in full) defines none of them. The editor's call sites pass no background to TooltipContent or DropdownMenuContent (design-editor.tsx:574-671). The Button base `inline-flex … whitespace-nowrap` and size icon-sm `size-8` (button.tsx:43, 77) are not generated. INFERRED rendering: menus and tooltips have no fill or shadow, and icon buttons collapse to glyph size. A rebuild alone does not fix this; the scan and the host CSS both need to change.

What I read: the host tokens are indigo on white/zinc (editor.css:15-35; dark mode 67-85 on hue 240). The website uses --primary 15 54% 46% (globals.css:79), and FLAT_UI §3.1 lists warm hue-30 darks (FLAT_UI.md:48-62). The header comment claiming 'the same values' (editor.css:4-6) is false. The shipped CSS uses var(--primary-ink), var(--destructive-ink) and var(--shadow-soft), but defines none of them. The generated rule is `.text-destructive{…color:hsl(var(--destructive-ink)/…)}`, which is invalid at computed-value time and so falls back to inherited colour. The native accent is user-selectable (JunoColors.swift:139-144), and no bridge command carries theme or accent (DesignHostCommand has only open/adopt/selection/readOnly).

What I read: exportAs calls fetch(`/api/design/${artifactId}/export…`) (design-editor.tsx:299-305). From file://…/index.html that resolves to file:///api/…, and the page CSP has `connect-src 'none'` (build-design-editor.mjs:105). bridge.ts does not intercept fetch; rg found no fetch in it. The Export menu renders unconditionally (design-editor.tsx:656-682). The failure lands in the catch as toast.error (340-341), and the Toaster is mounted (main.tsx:72). artifactId is the document id (main.tsx:66), which would be wrong even if fetch were allowed. The Design screen's ⋯ menu offers only Delete (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:486-497).

What I read: image placement goes through a hidden `<input type="file">` (design-canvas.tsx:1268-1276; inspector-panel.tsx:1275). The WKUIDelegate conformance implements only createWebViewWith (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:199-234), and I read the whole file: there is no runOpenPanelWith. On macOS, WKWebView shows no open panel unless the UI delegate provides one. rg found no onDrop or dataTransfer handling in design-canvas.tsx either. The ingest path, readImageAsset followed by onApply, is local and would work if a panel existed.

What I read: save() captures the draft (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:578), awaits saveArtifact, which covers the network call, merge, sync refresh and reload (NativeArtifactStore.swift:396-407), and then sets self.draft = nil unconditionally (581). Meanwhile onEdit keeps writing to draft (428). Edits made during that window drop out of the dirty state, while the canvas, which never re-reads content, still shows them. Mitigation: the next edit sets draft to the editor's full document again, including the dropped edits, so loss needs the user to leave right after the save. That is still possible, since leaving has no guard (mac-design-3). I lowered severity to low.

What I read: launcherContent branches only on designs.isEmpty (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:371-379) and never looks at model.phase. The scenario is narrower than claimed, though. On a sync failure, reload() still loads the local encrypted store, so a user with 30 local designs sees them (NativeArtifactStore.swift:258-288). 'No designs yet' appears only in three cases: before the model has loaded (artifactModel.start is awaited after the conversation, project and workspace models, JunoDesktopRootView.swift:195-207), on a fresh install before the first sync, or when the local store load throws (catch at 283-287, artifacts stay []).

What I read: HostedEditor passes no `surface` (main.tsx:65-71), so the default 'embedded' applies (design-editor.tsx:169). The rails, their collapsed stubs and their resize grips all use `hidden md:flex` / `hidden lg:flex` (549-550, 714, 720, 765, 826, 830, 870). The shipped CSS has those exact media rules, and the 17 Sept source had the same logic. Only design-workspace.tsx:213 uses surface="window". I raised severity because of the defaults: the main window opens at 1240pt (JunoDesktopApp.swift:148) and the Chat sidebar's ideal width is 264pt (JunoDesktopChrome.swift:47, applied by junoSidebarColumn). That leaves the detail column at about 975pt, below the 1024px lg breakpoint (INFERRED from the numbers; CSS px equal points at zoom 1). So at the default window size the inspector is hidden, with no control to bring it back.

What I read: every window `error` and `unhandledrejection` event, and React's onCaughtError, is posted as a failure (main.tsx:126-133). The host maps any failure to .failed (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:172-173). The surface draws an opaque JunoEmptyState over the web view with no retry (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1050-1054). Nothing moves the status back to .ready, and send() stops working because it is gated on .ready (141). The trigger is INFERRED. One plausible benign source is the ResizeObserver in design-canvas.tsx:221, since WebKit reports 'ResizeObserver loop completed…' as a window error. I kept severity low because I could not observe how often it happens.

What I read: the full host file implements decidePolicyFor, didFail, didFailProvisionalNavigation and createWebViewWith, and nothing else (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:199-234). There is no webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate, so after a content-process kill the status stays .ready and nothing reloads. The blank pane is INFERRED from standard WebKit behaviour.

What I read: the document view stacks documentCommandBar (Back, title/subtitle, Discard, Save, ⋯), then a Divider, then the editor (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:421-438, 442-501). The editor draws its own opaque toolbar row with `border-b … bg-card/40` (design-editor.tsx:554-706), holding tools, undo/redo, align, Motion, Export and Saving…. That gives two full-width chrome rows above the canvas. The Liquid Glass branch changes only doc comments and the sidebar icon in these files.

What I read: the web's httpTransport POSTs every transaction (use-design-document.ts:89-107), and the toolbar shows 'Saving…' (design-editor.tsx:691-697). bridgeTransport posts the whole document and returns ok immediately (bridge.ts:114-130), and the Mac needs a manual Save, with 'Unsaved changes' only in the caption subtitle (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:478-484, 503-510). The host's own comment contradicts the screen: it says 'Every transaction is already committed as it happens; an explicit save is a no-op' (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:167-170).

What I read: the host's dark palette is hue 240 zinc (editor.css:67-85), while FLAT_UI §3.1 specifies hue-30 warm darks (FLAT_UI.md:48-62). Accent resolution is user-driven through JunoAccentSelection (JunoColors.swift:139-144), and no host command carries theme or accent into the bundle.

What I read: Design is one switch arm inside the detail column (DesktopAccountScreens.swift:120-134). The only torn-off window is the library's read-only DesktopDesignSurface (DesktopArtifactsScreen.swift:1961-1967), and there is no focus or full-canvas mode. One nuance weakens 'no side-by-side designs': the main WindowGroup (JunoDesktopApp.swift:135) can open additional main windows (openWindow(id: mainID) at DesktopCommands.swift:108, DesktopMenuBarExtra.swift:46). Each window has its own Design screen state, so two designs can sit side by side, but each carries the full sidebar and chrome.

What I read: ⌘Z and the other chords fire only when document.activeElement is inside rootRef (design-editor.tsx:417-429). There is no undoRedo/pasteboard CommandGroup for design anywhere in native/macOS/JunoDesktop/App. Layer copy/paste exists only through the context menu's module-level clipboard (design-context-menu.tsx:59-78), and rg found no ⌘C/⌘V or copy/paste handler anywhere in src/components/design, on the web too. One nuance: clicking a SwiftUI button does not normally take first responder unless keyboard navigation is on, so 'after clicking Save' is a weak example. Clicking the sidebar or any native field does take focus, however, and ⌘Z then no longer reaches the editor.

missed.title: Native design saves bypass the design operation layer: the generic artifact POST stores any body without design validation
missed.evidence: READ: POST validates only `content: z.string().max(200_000)`, baseVersion and origin (route.ts:7-16, 47-49). It then writes the content verbatim as a new version (60-68), with no parse through the design schema for DESIGN artifacts. The design transactions route says 'This is the only write path. There is deliberately no "replace the document" endpoint: a client that could PUT a whole scene could also PUT one the operation layer never checked' (src/app/api/design/[artifactId]/transactions/route.ts:17-27). Yet the Mac and iPhone save designs as whole documents through this route (NativeArtifactAPIClient.swift:240-241 → saveArtifact, NativeArtifactStore.swift:321-335).
missed.failure_scenario: A native build whose codec has drifted, as with cornerSmoothing (mac-design-1), or a future bug that emits a structurally invalid scene, saves successfully. The server accepts it as the current version with no check. The web /design/[id] then either silently loses data or refuses to open a document the server itself stored, and version history is the only recovery.

missed.title: After a 409 the stale-save message says the latest version 'has been loaded', but the Design canvas never shows it
missed.evidence: READ: the .stale description is 'This artifact changed on another device. The latest version has been loaded.' (NativeArtifactAPIClient.swift:192-193). The Design screen shows it in the subtitle (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:508), keeps the draft (574-582), and the surface ignores the new content (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:973-979).
missed.failure_scenario: The user reads that the latest version was loaded, sees their own canvas unchanged, and presses Save again, which overwrites the other device's version (mac-design-2). The copy actively invites that data loss.

missed.title: Discard throws away all unsaved design work in one click, with no confirmation, right next to Save
missed.evidence: READ: Button("Discard") sets draft = nil and bumps designReloadToken, which remounts the editor and loses its undo stack (470-476). There is no confirmationDialog. Delete, by contrast, has an alert (265-277).
missed.failure_scenario: Aiming for Save, the user clicks the adjacent Discard. Every edit since the last save is gone, and so is the web editor's undo history, because the surface remounts with a new id.
